label: conj:whipple-rotation-intertwining
title: Whipple–rotation intertwining: the channel rotation acts on the toroidal family as the degree–order (winding) exchange
html:
Conjecture (Whipple–rotation intertwining). The archimedean shadow of the fibre-level channel rotation (x, q) \mapsto (ix, q^{-1}) acts on the toroidal channel family P^{\mu}_{\nu - 1/2}(\cosh\eta)\, e^{i\mu\theta} e^{i\nu\varphi} as the Whipple degree–order exchange: it swaps the two winding gradings (\mu, \nu) \mapsto (\nu, \mu) and is involutive on the ladder data.

Established results and open questions

The following supporting facts are verified (witness computations/substrate/whipple-rotation-involution-probe.witness.json):

  • the interpolating ladder is bar-even, [d]_{q^{-1}} = [d]_q (exact);
  • the Whipple argument exchange \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta is an exact involution, and the \zeta_4 quarter-period shift \cosh(t + i\pi/2) = i\sinh t maps the bar-even to the bar-odd channel;
  • numerically at 50 digits, the toroidal pair obeys
P^{-\mu}_{\nu-1/2}(\coth a)
= C(\nu, \mu)\, \sqrt{\sinh a}\;\, Q^{\nu}_{\mu-1/2}(\cosh a),

with a-independent C whose shift laws C(\nu, \mu+1)/C(\nu,\mu) = 1/(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) and C(\nu+1, \mu)/C(\nu,\mu) = -1/(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) carry a single \Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) with an alternating \nu-sign [whipple1917];

  • the constant's full Gamma structure is a symbolic-exact structural identity, grid-verified (not one-point): solving the two shift recurrences forces C(\nu,\mu) = \sqrt{2/\pi}\;e^{-i\pi\nu}/\Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}), which matches the direct 60-digit compute to \sim 10^{-40} across a grid of generic non-integer, non-half-integer (\nu,\mu) points (witness computations/substrate/whipple-gamma-constant-gridverify.witness.json);
  • the order \mu = \tfrac{1}{2} and the half-integer degree are forced by the Hoefsmit mixing structure (prop:hoefsmit-toroidal-ladder-locus);
  • the exchange holds at the physical forced windings themselves: at (\mu, \nu) = (\tfrac{1}{2}, d - \tfrac{1}{2}) for axial distances d \in \{2, 3, 4\} (the meson is d = 2) the same \Gamma-constant identity is exact to \sim 10^{-50} — not only at the generic grid points, which deliberately avoided the \mu = \tfrac{1}{2} order — and the order-ladder factor reproduces the mixing numerator d^2 - 1 at each d (witness computations/substrate/whipple-physical-windings-probe.witness.json). This is numerical evidence for the modeling layer, not a proof.

Open is the identification itself: that the channel rotation of the Ismail–Masson pair [ismail-masson1994] — the map carrying the bar-even recurrence to the bar-odd one — descends to the toroidal family as the Whipple exchange, i.e. that the two winding oscillations of a bound vortex pair are swapped by the substrate bar involution. The Lean sibling axiomatises exactly this as a primary conjecture class (WhippleRotationIntertwining): the rotation swaps the two winding gradings and is involutive on ladder data. Both fields are parameter-quantified in the shape of the claim; no instance is provided (the conjecture is open).

Two consequences are derived from the class (provable modulo it, no instance):

  • nuGrade_square — the along-loop winding is restored after a double rotation, so the winding pair (\mu, \nu) is fixed by \mathrm{rot}^2 (the categorical shadow of the exact \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta involution);
  • gradingPair_intertwines_swap — the winding-grading map x \mapsto (\mu(x), \nu(x)) intertwines the channel rotation with the coordinate swap: (\mu(\mathrm{rot}\,x), \nu(\mathrm{rot}\,x)) = \mathrm{swap}(\mu(x), \nu(x)). This is the exact discrete shadow of the Whipple degree–order exchange (\mu, \nu) \mapsto (\nu, \mu), and a genuine consequence of the two swap-component fields (not a restatement).

The archimedean amplitude of that exchange is fixed independently of the open identification: the grid-verified constant C(\nu,\mu) = \sqrt{2/\pi}\,e^{-i\pi\nu}/\Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) above is the symbolic-exact shadow the intertwining must carry.

The grading-swap field is moreover not primitive: channelIndexed_swaps_windings derives it from the even↔odd channel flip that prop on the channel rotation (rotation_step) proves. A ChannelIndexedLadder carries the two recurrence-channel indices, the rotation that flips them, and a single shared winding function \mathrm{windOf}; the swap \mathrm{windOf}(\mathrm{evenIdx}(\mathrm{rot}\,x)) = \mathrm{windOf}(\mathrm{oddIdx}\,x) then follows from the flip, not from an assumption. This does not close the conjecture (no instance is produced): it moves the open content off the swap and onto (i) identifying the abstract channel flip with rotation_step's \mathrm{oddStep} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{evenStep} carry, and (ii) the residual involutivity — the order-2 Whipple \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta exchange, a different map from the order-4 ζ₄ recurrence rotation, hence genuinely open.
